Each Monthly Update patch available on My Oracle Support is divided into a series of archive (ZIP) files. Depending on the Siebel Application Server operating system and the features you wish to deploy, you do not need to download all the files associated with the Monthly Update. The ZIP files provided in the Monthly Update will all have a name of the form p___.zip, where:
- refers to the MOS patch number for the Monthly Update. It will be an eight-digit number, such as 37386170.

Update Basics
A Monthly Update provides new product features and available fixes. Beyond this document, please review these related items:
- Installation instructions: For more about this Siebel CRM Update, including instructions for preparing the product media and for installing Siebel CRM, see the latest version of the _Installation Guide_ in _Siebel Bookshelf_ from the Siebel CRM Documentation site.
- Third-Party Certifications: For a list of Third-Party Certifications, please visit My Oracle Support and search for “Siebel Industry Applications” on the _Certifications_ tab.
- FAQ: The Siebel CRM Continuous Release Model (Doc ID 2378034.1).
NOTE: This document contains two years (24 months) of rolling content. For bug fixes and known issues in versions released before the scope of this document, please download earlier versions from Oracle Support (DOC ID 2382435.1).

Repository Updates
Some features require Repository, Seed, or Manifest changes in order to take advantage of the feature. These changes must be imported through execution of the _RepositoryUpdate_ utility in the Development environment. Please refer to the _Database Upgrade Guide_ for information on how to use RepositoryUpdate.
NOTE: Not all features require Repository changes. Examine the “Repository Update Required” column in the New Features tables below to see if such changes are required for a particular feature.

text:
various Siebel CRM utilities have used could introduce "table locks" or other conditions that would block end users from being able to use the application while the DDL was executing. When this occurred, downtime could occur during the application of Siebel Updates (PostInstallDBSetup or RepositoryUpgrade) and Migration operations.
Basic Technical Information
By modifying our existing utilities to leverage built-in capabilities of modern versions of the Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server database platforms, we can execute DDL that accomplishes the same end result without forcing downtime.
- For Oracle platforms, we leverage the DBMS_REDEFINITION package to make changes to objects without making any schema objects offline.
- For Microsoft SQL Server platforms, we leverage the "ONLINE" keyword to modify objects without bringing any schema objects offline.
For more information on the technical details of these database-level capabilities, please refer to the Oracle or Microsoft documentation as appropriate.
NOTE: This change is not applicable to either DB2 database platform.

Replacement of Obsolete Data Types from Oracle and MSSQL Databases This feature provides a utility to convert obsolete Column types, such as Oracle's LONG and Microsoft SQL Server's TEXT/NTEXT to their modern equivalents: CLOBs and VARCHAR(max)/NVARCHAR(max). The driver behind this is that the respective database vendors deprecated these data types a number of years ago and modern database engines are no longer being optimized for these older types. Siebel Cloud Manager - Smarter Ingress Routing Siebel Cloud Manager introduces support for Traefik as part of a Kubernetes deployment, to ensure continued security, support, and modern ingress traffic management. Support for Traefik is necessary as NGINX Ingress reaches end-of- life (March 2026). Traefik provides automatic SSL management, dynamic service discovery, and faster routing updates, reducing operational complexity. Its cloud-native design improves observability, scalability, and maintainability, and provides for the easy adoption of the Kubernetes Gateway API (a flexible, multi-protocol way to manage traffic routing). This enhancement ensures Siebel CRM deployments on Kubernetes remain secure, • Siebel Cloud Manager

text:
_Background_
User creation via the _User_ Integration Component of the _Users_ Integration Object fails as the Open API specification for the Integration Object does not have a required field _operation_ . This is because the _operation_ field is marked as a “system” field in the _User_ Integration Component definition, while the Siebel Open API specification only includes the fields that marked as “data”. To ensure the _operation_ field is included in the Open API specification, it must be changed to a Data field.
_Steps_
Repository Changes
Perform the following changes to convert the _operation_ field from “system” to “data”:
1. Select the _Users_ Integration Object.
2. Select the child Integration Component _User_ .
3. Select the child Integration Component Field _operation_ .
4. Modify the Type attribute to “Data”.
